rationale: The small espresso crossover gives individual differences in both directions and compares two brewed coffee conditions. The diet cohort combines coffee and tea. Two GBA-related cases report different coffee histories and current fatigue scores without assigned exposure or matched timing. Brewed coffee and Parkinson fatigue severity remain unresolved.

Dried rosemary capsule trials outside Parkinson disease favor lower depressive scores with baseline imbalance and completer limits in the major-depression trial. Fresh-derived drinks measured other acute ratings. A registered three-extract trial had inconclusive overall depression results and a favorable subgroup with unclear transfer to fresh rosemary alone. The weak lean against worsening still depends on transfer from dried capsules and other populations.

Parkinson cohorts and cases describe first onset, visual components of hallucinosis or illusions, and symptoms during medication treatment. The fig and olive trial and the dried fig allergy case do not measure visual episode frequency. Effects of eating dried figs in Parkinson disease remain unresolved.

Animal reports used fig extract or bark rather than raw fruit. Clinical Parkinson and Lewy body case series describe resting tremor without a food comparison, and one report’s description conflicts with its table. The direction for raw fig and Parkinson resting tremor severity remains unresolved.
